mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW X6 M60i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full BMW X6 M60i engine replacement typically costs £5,500-£9,500 supply-only for a rebuilt S68B44A unit, or £7,000-£11,000 fitted by a specialist. Used S68B44A engines: £3,500-£5,500 depending on mileage and condition. Reconditioned units: £4,500-£7,000. Professional fitting adds £1,500-£2,500 to the engine cost.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW X6 M60i S68 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The S68 is BMW's most advanced V8, incorporating racing technology from the XM and X7 M60i. However, early examples have reported oil pump failures - one owner needed a new engine at just 28,000 miles. The S68 is significantly more robust than the earlier N63 engines it replaces, but being a relatively new engine, long-term reliability data is still emerging. Regular oil changes and monitoring of the 48V system are essential.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of oil pump failure in a BMW X6 M60i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning signs of oil pump failure in the X6 M60i are: low oil pressure warning light - stop driving immediately; knocking or tapping noise from the engine; engine running rough or misfiring; complete engine seizure - if oil pressure drops to zero.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a BMW X6 M60i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an X6 M60i worth £55,000-£90,000, a £7,000-£11,000 rebuilt engine is typically good value - replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value. Compare replacement cost against vehicle value - replacement is viable up to approximately 70% of the car's value. Given the vehicle's high value, specialist rebuild with warranty is the safest option. Always factor the 12-month warranty into your replacement decision.

mainEntity.name: What causes the BMW X6 M60i 48V mild-hybrid system to fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 48V mild-hybrid system can fail due to: 48V lithium-ion battery degradation after 5-7 years (£600-£1,000 replacement); starter-generator belt wear or failure; battery management system faults. The system provides a temporary 12hp and 200Nm boost under acceleration. If the system fails, the engine loses electric boost and coasting functionality.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my BMW X6 M60i engine with a different engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Engine swaps to a different size or type are technically complex and rarely cost-effective for the X6 M60i. The S68B44A and S68B44T0 are the only engines fitted to the M60i from the factory - stick to like-for-like replacement. Swapping to the X6 M Competition engine (S63B44C) requires different ECU, wiring, cooling, and transmission calibration. The 48V mild-hybrid system is integrated with the engine - swapping to a non-hybrid engine is not feasible. Insurance must be notified of any non-standard engine swap. Our marketplace only recommends like-for-like code-matching for warranty coverage.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW X6 M60i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW X6 M60i arrived in 2023 as the G06 facelift's new flagship petrol model, replacing the M50i. Powered by the S68 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8 - the most advanced hot-vee V8 BMW has ever produced - the M60i sits between the xDrive40i and the full-fat X6 M Competition, offering M-division engineering with everyday usability.

milestones.description: April 2023 - BMW X6 M60i (G06 LCI) launches with the S68B44A 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8, producing 530hp (390kW) and 750Nm of torque, paired with a 48V mild-hybrid system
X6 M60i receives updated engine calibration; power remains 530hp with 48V mild hybrid assistance providing 12hp temporary boost
Current production continues with S68B44T0 engine code for UK market cars

commonProblems.h2: BMW X6 M60i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW X6 M60i is powered by the S68 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8 - BMW's most advanced hot-vee V8, featuring a 48V mild-hybrid system and M-division engineering. While significantly more robust than the earlier N63 engines it replaces, the S68 is not without its teething issues. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Pump Failure - Why the BMW X6 M60i S68 Loses Oil Pressure
problems.rootCause: The S68's high-performance oil pump system - while incorporating racing technology with a modified oil pump and sump system and strengthened crankshaft drive - has shown vulnerability on some early G06 M60i examples. One owner reported needing a new engine and turbos at just 28,000 miles. Oil pump failure leads to low oil pressure, bearing damage, and ultimately catastrophic engine failure if not addressed immediately.

With a full rebuilt engine costing £7,000-£11,000 fitted, replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value - making engine replacement a financially viable option for most M60i owners. However, given the vehicle's high value, using a specialist with S68 experience is essential to protect your investment.
problems.recommendation: If you see any low oil pressure warning on your X6 M60i, stop driving immediately and have the oil system inspected. Early intervention can save the engine. Given the high value of the vehicle, a specialist oil pump replacement (£1,800-£3,000) is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Always use the correct BMW-approved oil specification and maintain strict oil change intervals.

problems.h4: 48V Mild-Hybrid System Failure - Why the BMW X6 M60i Loses Electric Assist
problems.rootCause: The 48V mild-hybrid system provides a temporary 12hp and 200Nm boost. The 48V lithium-ion battery can degrade over time, and the starter-generator belt can wear. When the system fails, the engine loses its electric boost, coasting functionality, and smooth stop-start operation. Fuel economy drops by approximately 8%.

repairOptions.longevity: Required if charging system faults appear

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - rebuilt/reconditioned engine (if electrical fault caused engine damage - rare)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt S68 with new MHEV components, 12-month warranty

problems.recommendation: The 48V system is a separate component from the engine block and can be replaced individually. If you notice reduced performance, stop-start not working, or warning lights, have the MHEV system diagnosed. Battery replacement at a specialist for £600-£1,000 is the most common fix. Do not ignore MHEV warnings - a failing starter-generator can leave you stranded.

problems.group: Oil Consumption & False Low Oil Warnings
problems.h4: Oil Consumption & False Low Oil Warnings - Why the BMW X6 M60i S68 Shows Oil Alerts
problems.rootCause: The S68, like its N63 predecessors, can consume oil at a higher rate than typical engines - a characteristic of the hot-vee V8 design. Additionally, a DME calibration error can trigger false low oil level warnings if a manual oil measurement has not been performed for an extended period, which is common in vehicles with frequent short-distance driving profiles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Update DME software to address false low oil warnings
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if warnings are false positives

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Top up oil to correct level, perform manual oil measurement
repairOptions.longevity: Regular maintenance - check oil every 1,000 miles

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - valve stem seal replacement (if oil consumption exceeds 1L/1,000 miles)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve stem seals with upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil consumption becomes excessive

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - rebuilt/reconditioned engine (if oil starvation caused damage)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt S68 with upgraded seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation caused bearing damage

problems.recommendation: On an X6 M60i worth £55,000-£90,000, regular oil checks are essential. Check the oil level manually every 1,000 miles - do not rely solely on the electronic sensor. If you see low oil warnings, have the DME software updated to rule out false positives. If oil consumption exceeds 1 litre per 1,000 miles, valve stem seal replacement at a specialist (£2,500-£4,000) is significantly cheaper than waiting for engine damage.
